Emergency medicine · published research

Snakebite

When added to antivenom, PBM reduced pain, swelling, limb circumference, and creatine kinase at 48 hours in one randomized trial. Infection, necrosis, analgesic use, and later disability did not differ.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

When added to antivenom, PBM reduced pain, swelling, limb circumference, and creatine kinase at 48 hours in one randomized trial. Infection, necrosis, analgesic use, and later disability did not differ.

Summary of the Evidence

Thirty-eight publications are included in a narrow snake-envenomation map: one double-blind randomized human trial, one systematic review, and 36 distinct preclinical primary reports. The preclinical set contains 25 animal reports and 12 in-vitro reports, with one mixed paper included in both counts. One additional nerve-repair paper using snake-derived fibrin glue is excluded because it did not study envenomation. The mapped studies span different venoms, models, and outcomes.

Human and clinical evidence

In the randomized trial, 60 people bitten by Bothrops atrox received standard antivenom with either PBM or the comparator treatment. At 48 hours, the PBM group had lower creatine kinase, a marker of muscle injury, less pain, a smaller increase in limb circumference, and less edema. Temperature difference between limbs, secondary infection, necrosis, use of pain medication, and later disability outcomes did not differ between groups. No adverse events were reported (Carvalho et al. 2024).

Animal evidence

Across the animal reports, most Bothrops models found reduced edema, hemorrhage, muscle-fibre injury, or pain sensitivity after PBM. Some studies also describe more muscle regeneration or return of enzyme markers toward baseline. Results vary by venom, wavelength, timing, and outcome; not every measure moved in the same direction. The systematic review summarizes 16 animal experiments, many of which also appear among the primary publications, so it is not an extra set of animals.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

The in-vitro reports mainly expose macrophages, muscle-related cells, or other cell preparations to venom or venom components. They report improved cell survival or mitochondrial activity in some experiments, lower oxidative stress or cytotoxicity, and changes in inflammatory signaling. One mixed paper contributes to both the animal and in-vitro counts.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The human trial used red and infrared LED emitters at 4 J/cm² for about 40 seconds per treatment point, in addition to antivenom. Exact wavelength and irradiance details are not consistently reported in the database summary. Animal studies include red visible wavelengths and near-infrared light, with differing doses and treatment timing. No clinical head-to-head study identifies an optimal protocol or shows that the same regimen works for other venom species.

Interpretation

The direct trial found less early pain and local swelling, alongside lower creatine kinase, when PBM was added to antivenom. It did not find lower necrosis, infection, analgesic use, or later disability. Animal and cell results often point in the same direction for local tissue injury, but do not extend the clinical finding to long-term function. PBM in these studies is an adjunct to antivenom, not a substitute for it.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow-to-moderate for early pain, edema, and muscle-injury markers when PBM is added to antivenom Low for effects on necrosis, infection, and later disability
Publications and records38 relevant articles (one mixed animal/in-vitro paper)

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

A double-blind randomized trial found lower pain, swelling, and creatine kinase at 48 hours when PBM was added to antivenom. Those direct patient outcomes support a treatment effect on early local injury. The same trial found no difference in necrosis, infection, analgesic use, or later disability. Replication across venom types and centres, with longer follow-up, would support stronger conclusions.
